case.question: What does DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT mean, and what should I inspect?
expected_points: pool usage versus 20, waiters and acquisition latency

chunk.title: Database connection-pool exhaustion runbook (synthetic)
chunk.text:
Database connection-pool exhaustion runbook (synthetic) | Distinguishing checks
DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT means order-api waited 500 ms for a pool slot. Compare db_pool_in_use with the per-process limit of 20, db_pool_waiters, and db_pool_acquire_ms for the same process and time window. A full pool with waiting requests supports investigating pool contention; it does not prove that PostgreSQL itself is unavailable. The error differs from DEPENDENCY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, which describes waiting for inventory-api rather than acquiring a database connection.

chunk.title: Inventory dependency timeout runbook (synthetic)
chunk.text:
Inventory dependency timeout runbook (synthetic) | Distinguishing checks
DEPENDENCY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT means the order-api inventory client exceeded its 1500 ms request deadline. Inspect dependency_name, upstream_status, inventory_request_ms and trace spans for the same request_id and time window. A missing upstream_status can mean no response was received before the deadline; it does not establish whether inventory-api completed the operation. Compare database pool metrics separately: DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT indicates waiting for a database slot, not an inventory response.

chunk.title: Error identifier reference (synthetic)
chunk.text:
Error identifier reference (synthetic) | Error meanings
DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT: waiting longer than 500 ms for an order-api PostgreSQL pool slot. DEPENDENCY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: the order-api inventory request exceeds 1500 ms. These describe different stages; neither code proves an underlying cause. A 503 returned to the order caller is shared by multiple failures and is insufficient for diagnosis.

DB_POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT means order-api waited 500 ms for a pool slot.
